Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *yuHs-
Proto-Balto-Slavic *jáušāˀ
Proto-Slavic *jūxà
Old East Slavic уха (uxa)
Russian уха́ (uxá)bor.
English ukha
Borrowed from Russian уха́ (uxá). Doublet of jus and juice.
q: You’ll see pools of kefir, sbiten, kvass, or vzvar in cavities of rocks, borscht and ukha swelling up in tree stumps, stuffed blintzes and pierogi mushrooming in flower clusters or out of tree bark or hanging from leaves, and cream-covered smetannik adorning trees like snow.
